resources.string: Search apps, components, or package names
An older module is still running / update not completed
Configuration needs checking; tap to view status
View selected rules with no current match
Manage system candidate entries here. Use Help in the list summary to see the current category and its limits. Selection changes are staged until Apply changes is confirmed.
Current mode: Hide selected. Checked entries are hidden from the corresponding candidate list; uncheck them to restore normal visibility.
Current mode: Show selected only. Checked entries are kept and other matching entries are hidden.
Current mode: Show all. Candidate filtering is paused while saved rules remain. New selections require Apply changes confirmation and do not filter candidates while this mode is active.
Checked means hide or retain according to the global mode, not set as Android default. Rule selections require Apply confirmation. Unlock locked entries from the three-dot menu before selecting them.

Editing dedicated rules for “Open · %1$s”. Effective selections combine the generic OPEN rules from All with rules dedicated to the current type. Inherited items remain selected and show their source when expanded. Inherited items must be deselected under All; rules added for the current type affect only that MIME, scheme, or file-extension type.
system has confirmed that filtering, ordering, and custom display names are paused; the configuration is retained
Paused locally; system application has not yet been confirmed
Categories with no selections temporarily show all candidates
This refresh was incomplete. Check scan details under Settings - Scanning & Refresh and refresh again.
Controls whether selected candidate entries are hidden, kept, or temporarily ignored. It does not choose system defaults.

Saving locally does not mean the system has applied the configuration. Use the configuration acknowledgement as the source of truth; final behavior still needs real-device verification on the relevant system or app surface.
No acknowledgement for the current configuration yet
Ordering rewrites recorded by system processes: %1$d

Query and app-visibility counts come from actual system_server execution. Ordering and some chooser surfaces run in separate Resolver/Chooser processes, so a count of 0 alone does not prove a rule is broken. Diagnostic mode can record Resolver-side delivery; verify the final UI on the device.

Compatibility fallback for source apps whose own candidate lists bypass normal Resolver rules, such as some file managers. For selected source apps, target packages from supported package-visibility scopes can be hidden at PackageManager level.
Selections are saved immediately and only apply in Hide selected mode. This runs in android/system_server and hides the whole target package from the source app; it cannot hide only one Activity.

Scans discover manageable candidates and may not match the current system menu. Shortcut and Direct Share sources include runtime Hook observations, proactive read-only scans and history. Proactive candidates are not proof of final display. Privileged system calls and OEM menus may bypass rules.
Preview final open targets with an actual file

When enabled, records query categories, rules, and skip reasons, including the first valid query stack by category and calling UID. Management scans do not consume stack records. Runtime logs avoid full filenames, URIs, or shortcut IDs. Key records are rate-limited to keep diagnostics bounded.
Diagnostics enabled; reproduce the entry, chooser, shortcut, provider, or service-candidate behavior you want to inspect.

Enable diagnostics first, reproduce the problem, then export. The package includes recent LSPosed and system logs where available. Raw system logs can contain data from other processes, so review before sharing. Root access is required for some sources; read failures are recorded in the package.

No runtime observation for this entry yet. Invoke it in the target app or launcher and refresh. If proactive discovery is enabled, scan candidates under Settings - Scanning & Refresh; those are not necessarily the final menu.
Some candidates could not be scanned. Refresh to retry.
No candidates have been discovered yet. Refresh or check module permissions.
No entries match the current filters.
Some entries are unavailable or restricted
No request-matched DocumentsUI roots were captured. Historical roots are diagnostic only, not the current Open/Save list.
DocumentsUI returned these roots for this action. MIME type and root capabilities can still affect the final sidebar.
No post-filter manager return was confirmed for this caller. Use Show API to inspect candidates; they are not the cleaned system list.
Some recommended LSPosed scopes are not granted (module may still work)
Could not read applications in the selected Android space. An empty list is not confirmed; check Root access and retry.
This import restores rules only. Root-disabled components are recorded for reference and are never changed automatically.
Only a related system settings screen can be opened when the OEM picker is unavailable. This is not a verified Autofill provider list.
Opens Android Default apps settings. Optional Intent testing is separate and may open an application; neither is proof of the filtered system list.
Long-press the sample text below and select some text to open Android\'s real text-selection menu. Available Process Text actions depend on the text editor and device.
Shortcut items are controlled by ShortcutService and the launcher. There is no public system list picker; inspect Hook observations instead.
Opens a system document/photo picker. Its content is not the complete list of providers or sidebar entries; consult captured host results.
Opens the Android Settings entry for this feature, not the actual Hook-filtered service list.
Opens an Android test scenario, not necessarily the exact menu used by another app. API candidates and Hook observations remain separate.
Android does not expose a general public Quick Settings tile editor to third-party apps. The installed tile catalog is not the SystemUI edit panel.
Opens the system widget picker using a temporary List Cleaner widget host. Selection is discarded and the temporary ID is released; it is not the launcher\'s widget drawer.
Opens a generic Android chooser, not the launcher\'s actual app or shortcut panel.
This system-owned list has no supported public launcher. Only available API candidates or runtime observations can be inspected.
This system entry belongs to a different Android user. Cross-user UI launch is restricted; only the current user can be tested here.
No verified current system list is available for this entry. Use Show API for candidates or inspect prior Hook observations.
This device does not provide an accessible system widget picker.
Data source: captured Hook return (not guaranteed to match the final rendered UI)
Data source: API candidates, not final system list
Data source: DocumentsUI matching roots for this operation
Data source: no verified system return for this request
Open the native Android input-method switcher. This popup lists enabled keyboards; the system settings button manages installation and activation.
This device does not support the dedicated settings page. A broader related page was opened instead.
Data source: observed system Settings UID Hook return (shared UIDs do not prove the final rendered list)
DocumentsUI returned roots, but its request action could not be identified (action=%1$s; state=%2$s). The result is history, not a verified Open/Save list.
Source: enabled services or current RoleManager holders; not a complete on-screen list
Source: previously observed runtime entries; not current system visibility
Previous DocumentsUI roots are available in History. They are not part of this test.
Partial capture: system returned %1$d items; %2$d were stored. The missing entries were not removed by filtering.
Credential Provider cleanup has been retired. Legacy backup entries remain readable but are not filtered, sorted, or presented as active ListCleaner entries.

AutofillService candidates are scanned independently and are not a verified enabled or visible list. Recent AOSP Settings merges Autofill with Credential Manager in one picker; the button launches that native AOSP page when available and otherwise falls back to public related Settings.

Uses Root to discover the actual Android PermissionController role picker and verify the foreground Activity after launch. No assistant is changed. If the device blocks the role picker, an error is shown instead of silently opening the assistant settings parent. You may open that settings page separately.
The protected assistant chooser is unavailable. Opening Assistant settings instead; select Default digital assistant to see the eligible apps.
Unable to query the system assistant picker. Check Root authorization and the diagnostic log; no substitute page was opened.
No PermissionController assistant role picker was found for this user. Open assistant settings and select Default digital assistant app instead.
Android refused to launch the assistant role picker. See ListCleaner.SystemPreview diagnostics. Nothing was changed.
OxygenOS redirected the assistant picker back to Settings. This is not the actual assistant list. Use Open assistant settings and tap the first row.
The assistant role picker request was sent, but its final foreground screen could not be verified. Check system diagnostics rather than assuming success.
Record system logs across Android users with Root (up to about 30 MB). Switch profiles to reproduce the issue, then stop. Logs may include sensitive information.
Recording in progress. Switch to the other user, reproduce the issue and return to stop.
Root log operation failed. Check Root authorization.
Recorded files are included in the full diagnostic ZIP.
Notification dismissal and stale rule maintenance

Only shows active notifications after permission is granted. Dismissal actually removes notifications; it does not silently hide them. Ongoing, foreground-service, call and alarm notifications are protected. Channel rows are active-channel observations, not the complete registered channel list.
Grant notification access in Android Settings
Access is enabled, but the notification listener is not connected. Check the service status.
Requested dismissal of %1$d notifications; some may have already disappeared.
This will remove %1$d active notifications. It is not a UI-only hide, and cannot be undone.

Full-scan the current user profile, then review rules whose items could not be found. Missing results may be caused by system query restrictions; only remove rules you recognize. Locked rules remain protected.
The scan failed; no rules can be removed.
Remove %1$d rules in the currently selected profile? This does not uninstall apps or delete their files.
Registered device-control services only. This is not a verified SystemUI controls panel list.
Choose apps to hide in one AOSP list only. No app is disabled, no task is stopped, and no file is deleted. This relies on the exact AOSP runtime classes and may require a process restart.
%1$d additional matches; refine search to see them
These filters affect SystemUI, Settings, Launcher3 or DocumentsUI presentation only. A running process may require restart. Continue?

Hide a specific channel in the AOSP notification shade without disabling its app or deleting notifications. A complete channel inventory requires associated-device or notification-assistant privilege; otherwise only channels observed in active notifications can be shown.
Restricted access: only channels observed in active notifications. Unseen channels are not shown.
Only notification shade display is filtered. Channel importance and saved notifications are not changed.
Current notifications, notification shade and channels
App drawer, suggestions and recent task cards
Quick Settings, recent files, app management and media devices
Review invalid rules before removing them
Hide selected applications in the notification shade, without dismissing posted notifications
Hide selected apps from the AOSP app drawer without disabling launch activities
Filter recent task cards without stopping running tasks
Hide or prioritize available tiles in the add-tile editor
Filter recent file sources in AOSP DocumentsUI
Hide or prioritize rows in the AOSP installed-app list
Hide unconnected media output destinations from the device list
Select notifications in the list; protected items stay visible but cannot be dismissed.
Browse current notifications by Android message, email, call, alarm and other categories
